claims.statement: The prod reboot posture is a two-round history: feature 028's repo-side fixes (broad 0.0.0.0 binds, an idempotent Mongo keyfile entrypoint, an assumed-correct restart policy) were followed by feature 029 superseding 028's own port assignment, and feature 030 fixing two further root causes exposed by a 2026-07-08 validation reboot; the drain unit starts the chain because it deliberately stops every container cleanly on shutdown, so boot begins from every container Exited (0).

A published port scoped to the tailnet IP silently fails to bind because the rootless Docker daemon starts before tailscaled, leaving the container Up with an empty Ports column and nothing listening; a plain container restart does not recover it, only a 0.0.0.0 bind or a full rootless-daemon restart after tailscaled is up, and tailnet-only exposure is then preserved solely by the host ufw default-deny posture.

Feature 028's own 0.0.0.0:8099 Keycloak admin bind was superseded by feature 029 because prod and the CI runner are two rootless daemons publishing into one host port space: 0.0.0.0:8099 collided with the CI app-e2e Keycloak's 127.0.0.1:8099, so a live CI Keycloak (once a leftover stack for ~6h) crash-looped prod auth on redeploy; the three prod admin/UI publishes therefore moved into the prod-reserved range 19000-19099.

Feature 029 made the intra-stack keycloak-network compose-managed instead of external, so compose creates and attaches Keycloak and its Postgres atomically on every up; this closed a worse failure than a partial re-attach, where a failed port bind rolled back keycloak-service's networking entirely and it could not resolve its own Postgres (UnknownHostException).

restart: unless-stopped cannot bring a container back on this host because the graceful-shutdown drain unit stops every container to Exited (0), and unless-stopped declines to restart a container that was already stopped when the daemon starts; proven on Docker 29.6.0, and the fix is restart: always on every prod compose service and every host-managed compose, with one-shot init containers idling on sleep infinity so they stay eligible.

The graceful-shutdown drain unit had to be reworked to stop containers in parallel: sequentially running docker stop -t 30 over roughly 40 containers exceeded TimeoutStopSec=120 and was SIGKILL'd mid-drain, stopping a non-deterministic subset, whereas parallel stopping completes within the timeout because restart: always now guarantees the return.

Komodo periphery's root_directory default /etc/komodo sits on a per-daemon tmpfs under rootless Docker (RootlessKit --copy-up=/etc), so the cloned repo checkout that every stack's relative bind-mounts resolve against is wiped on every reboot; Docker then auto-creates each missing bind-mount source file as a directory, failing the Mongo and Vault containers with 'not a directory' and exit 127. The fix is host state: point PERIPHERY_ROOT_DIRECTORY at persistent disk and recreate periphery.

A crash-looping non-root Mongo keyfile entrypoint is a permissions bug rather than a data bug: mongo-entrypoint.sh writes the replica-set keyfile at 0400, a plain container restart leaves the prior run's read-only file in place, and non-root mongod cannot reopen it for write (EACCES), so the fix removes the file before rewriting it on every start, making the operation idempotent.

The keyfile idempotency regression test must run as a non-root uid or it masks the bug: mongo-entrypoint.test.sh drives the real entrypoint script with a no-op exec target and explicitly plants a pre-existing 0400 keyfile to reproduce the restart case, with the harness noting that root would bypass the permission failure.

A durable network re-attach after a reboot is a Komodo redeploy, not a manual docker network connect: the prod-auth compose already declares keycloak-service on backend-network, so a ResourceSync redeploy recreates the container with its full declared network set, while a manual docker network connect is a one-off the next reboot can lose.

Komodo's own periphery agent is a recovery dependency, not just a deployed workload: periphery runs as a rootless container that the drain stops, so Komodo Core loses its agent on reboot and cannot redeploy anything, and Komodo clones the repo from Forgejo on every sync — the manual recovery order is start periphery, start Forgejo, then Execute Sync.

The tailnet throughput collapse was a host-level segmentation-offload bug on the tailnet interface, not a network fault: it was direction-asymmetric (bulk outbound capped around 150 KB/s while receive ran at ~15 MB/s), left small-packet latency, loss and every counter clean, and the decisive tell was that no plausible network condition could produce the measured number; the fix must be bound to interface recreation via a device-keyed systemd unit because both a reboot and a tailscaled restart reset it.

scripts/check-prod-ci-port-collision.mjs enforces prod/CI port disjointness by comparing host port NUMBERS and ignoring host_ip, because a prod 0.0.0.0 bind collides with a CI bind on the same number whatever interface the CI side names; it skips entries with no deterministic fixed host port (bare container port or ${VAR} host field), expands numeric ranges, and exits 0 clean / 1 collision / 2 unparseable with a --selftest that plants an overlap.

scripts/check-prod-restart-policy.mjs makes restart: always a required, self-enforcing property of every service in every infrastructure-as-code/docker/**/compose.prod.yaml: unless-stopped is forbidden as the round-2 regression, a missing restart: is forbidden because it defaults to no, and no/on-failure are allowed only for one-shot init/seed containers whose names match the init/seed/createbucket pattern.

Both reboot-resilience gates run selftest-then-scan as required guardrails in the naming job of .forgejo/workflows/guardrails.yml on every PR and push to main, and are also run locally by scripts/preflight.mjs, so a collision or a drifted restart policy is caught before reaching prod rather than via an outage.

The restart-policy fix is only durable as config-as-code: an interim `docker update --restart always` over the running containers is lost as soon as any container is recreated by a Komodo redeploy, a compose `up`, or a host rebuild, so durability comes from the committed prod compose value plus the host-managed compose edits.

Host-managed composes (Forgejo, Komodo, cloudflared and the monitoring stack) live outside the repository, so no repo gate can fail on their restart policy — their `restart: always` is host state an operator maintains by hand, and a rebuild that omits it reintroduces the round-2 failure for those stacks only.

The reboot posture depends on host state no gate can see: the graceful-shutdown drain unit, a UPS/NUT orderly-shutdown trigger for sustained power loss, backups covering all data volumes rather than a subset, and the device-keyed tailnet segmentation-offload unit — the source runbook's host-remediation table is the authoritative record with a verification command per control.

scripts/check-prod-ci-port-collision.mjs splits the tree by filename: prod is every compose file whose basename ends `.prod.yaml`, and CI/dev is every other tracked compose file (compose.yaml, compose.ci.yaml, compose.agent-e2e.yaml, stacks/*.compose.yaml), so disjointness is enforced across that file classification rather than a declared list.

Both bind-prefix variables were retired only after their consumers went away: `KC_ADMIN_BIND_IP` was only ever the Keycloak admin bind prefix, feature 028 dropped it from the compose bind, and Komodo kept passing it to the `prod-auth` stack until 2026-10-12 (item #727) — so until then it reached the container through the compose `env_file:` as a `KC_*` variable naming no Keycloak option; `TS_ADMIN_IP` was only the prefix of the two observability operator-UI binds, feature 028 made those binds `0.0.0.0`, and the stack stopped passing it on 2026-10-13 (item #727). No stack or compose file reads either now, so both Komodo Variables can be retired, and retiring the stack `environment` line together with the Variable is the rule.

A prod published-port move is not complete when the compose bind changes, because the collision gate only reads a compose file's `ports:` key and never the self-referencing URL variables: Keycloak's `KC_HOSTNAME_ADMIN` and LangFuse's `NEXTAUTH_URL` must be moved in the same change, or the service binds cleanly while serving a URL for the old port — a working bind with a broken redirect that no port-scan gate can see.

The tailnet segmentation-offload fix is durable only because it is bound to device creation: the device-bound systemd unit re-applies `ethtool -K tailscale0 tso off gso off gro off` whenever the tun appears, because a `tailscaled` restart recreates the tun and resets the flags exactly as a reboot does; verification is `ethtool -k tailscale0` reading the three offloads `off`, and the residual risk is a race in which Tailscale re-enables TSO/GSO on its own tun.

The tailnet throughput diagnosis had two measurement traps that manufactured false conclusions: PowerShell `Invoke-WebRequest` measured roughly 40x slower than `curl.exe` on the same fetch (1.57 MB/s vs 68.6 MB/s), and a tailnet shell session is Tailscale SSH, which terminates inside `tailscaled` and never traverses `tailscale0`, so its download path sits near 10 KB/s and did not improve with the offload fix — it must not be used as a throughput probe.
